plugin.name: iOS
plugin.description: Xcode workspace and project detection, build and install to devices or simulators, CocoaPods and Swift packages, signing and device diagnostics, TestFlight upload
opt.device.info: When empty: use the only connected device if exactly one is available; otherwise use a booted simulator.
opt.args.info: Appended after the launch arguments enabled in the scheme.
opt.env.info: Passed to the app process (merged with the environment variables enabled in the scheme).
opt.container.info: When empty: a CocoaPods workspace is always used; otherwise the one Xcode opened most recently, so incremental builds are shared through DerivedData; otherwise the workspace is preferred.
setting.allowProvisioning: Allow Xcode to update certificates and profiles
setting.allowProvisioning.info: Pass -allowProvisioningUpdates to xcodebuild for device builds, archives and exports: certificates and provisioning profiles are created and devices registered with the Apple account signed in to Xcode, just like pressing Run in Xcode.
action.testflight.confirm: The default scheme (the first run configuration) will be archived with its archive configuration (usually Release) and uploaded to App Store Connect using the Apple account signed in to Xcode. Uploads cannot be undone; the build appears in TestFlight after processing. Continue?
form.method.info: Development: installs only on development devices included in the profile. Ad Hoc: installs on registered test devices, signed with a distribution certificate.
deps.pods.missing: pod install has not been run
deps.pods.outdated: Pods are out of sync with Podfile.lock; run pod install again
deps.spm.unresolved: No Package.resolved yet; xcodebuild resolves packages on the first build
msg.uploaded: {0} was uploaded to App Store Connect and will appear in TestFlight after processing. Archive: {1}
err.noContainer: No Xcode workspace or project in this folder
err.noXcode: Xcode is not available. Install Xcode from the App Store and make sure xcode-select points to Xcode, not CommandLineTools.
err.noDevice: No device available: connect an iPhone / iPad with a cable and trust this computer on the device, or boot a simulator.
err.multipleDevices: {0} devices are connected. Choose one in the run configuration.
err.deviceNotFound: Device {0} not found: it may be disconnected, locked, or on a different network.
err.deviceUnavailable: Device "{0}" is not reachable: connect it with a cable, or keep it unlocked on the same network as this Mac.
err.deviceNotPaired: Device "{0}" does not trust this computer yet: unlock it, tap Trust in the "Trust This Computer?" alert and enter the passcode.
err.developerMode: Developer Mode is off on "{0}": turn it on in Settings > Privacy & Security > Developer Mode, restart the device as prompted, then run again.
err.osTooOld: "{0}" runs iOS {1}, but the app requires iOS {2}.
err.settings: Failed to read build settings (exit code {0}): {1}
err.bundleId: Could not read the bundle ID of {0}
err.noPod: The pod command was not found. Install CocoaPods first: brew install cocoapods
err.upload: Uploading to App Store Connect failed (exit code {0})
fix.installXcode: Install Xcode from the App Store
confirm.downloadPlatform: This runs xcodebuild -downloadPlatform iOS to download the iOS platform components (several GB). It may take a while. Continue?
diag.noXcode.title: Xcode is not installed
diag.noXcode.message: Building and running iOS apps needs the full Xcode (the command line tools are not enough). Open Xcode once after installing to finish installing components.
diag.xcodeSelect.title: xcode-select points to the command line tools
diag.xcodeSelect.message: The active developer directory is {0}, which xcodebuild cannot use. Let Lemon Paperplane use Xcode (recommended), or run in Terminal: {1}
diag.xcodeSelectLog.message: The active developer directory is {1}, not Xcode. Let Lemon Paperplane use /Applications/Xcode.app, or run in Terminal: sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer
diag.license.title: The Xcode license has not been accepted
diag.license.message: Open Xcode once and accept the license, or run in Terminal: {0}
diag.licenseLog.message: Open Xcode once and accept the license, or run in Terminal: sudo xcodebuild -license accept
diag.firstLaunch.title: Xcode first-launch components are not installed
diag.firstLaunch.message: Open Xcode once and install the components, or run in Terminal: {0}
diag.noScheme.title: No runnable scheme
diag.noScheme.message: {0} has no scheme that runs an iOS app. Create one in Xcode, or check Shared in Manage Schemes.
diag.noTeamStatic.title: "{0}" has no development team
diag.noTeamStatic.message: Installing on a device requires signing. Choose a team under Signing & Capabilities in Xcode; you can ignore this if you only use simulators.
diag.buildFailed.title: Build failed
diag.buildFailed.message: See the console for errors; open in Xcode for the full issue list.
diag.pickDevice.title: Choose a run destination
diag.pickDevice.message: {0} devices are connected. Choose one to run on (saved in this run configuration).
diag.deviceNotFound.title: The selected device was not found
diag.deviceNotFound.message: Device {0} is disconnected, locked, or on a different network.
diag.deviceUnavailable.title: "{0}" is not reachable
diag.deviceUnavailable.message: Connect the device with a cable, or keep it unlocked on the same network as this Mac.
diag.notPaired.title: "{0}" does not trust this computer
diag.notPaired.message: Unlock the device, tap Trust in the "Trust This Computer?" alert and enter the passcode. If no alert appears, reconnect the cable.
diag.notPairedLog.title: The device does not trust this computer
diag.developerMode.title: Developer Mode is off on "{0}"
diag.developerModeLog.title: Developer Mode is off on the device
diag.developerMode.message: On the device, turn on Settings > Privacy & Security > Developer Mode and restart as prompted; after restarting, unlock the device and confirm. If the switch is missing, run on this device from Xcode once.
diag.osTooOld.title: "{0}" runs an older iOS ({1})
diag.osTooOld.message: The app requires iOS {0} or later. Use another device, or lower the deployment target in Xcode.
diag.noDevice.title: No device available
diag.noDevice.message: Connect an iPhone / iPad with a cable and trust this computer, or install an iOS simulator in Xcode > Settings > Components and boot one.
diag.noTeam.title: "{1}" has no development team
diag.noTeam.message: Choose a team for this target under Signing & Capabilities in Xcode (sign in to your Apple account in Xcode > Settings > Accounts first), then retry.
diag.noProfiles.title: No provisioning profile for {1}
diag.noProfiles.message: Xcode has no provisioning profile for this bundle ID. Make sure Xcode is signed in to the team account and Automatically manage signing is checked; this also happens when "Allow Xcode to update certificates and profiles" is turned off.
diag.noAccount.title: Xcode has no account for team {1}
diag.noAccount.message: Open Xcode > Settings > Accounts, sign in with an Apple account in this team, then retry.
diag.noCertificate.title: Signing certificate "{1}" is missing
diag.noCertificate.message: The keychain has no usable signing certificate (or private key) for this team. Create one in Xcode > Settings > Accounts > Manage Certificates, or export it from the Mac that created it.
diag.notRegistered.title: The device is not registered in the developer account
diag.notRegistered.message: This device is not in the team's device list. Retry with "Allow Xcode to update certificates and profiles" on to register it automatically; if your role cannot register devices, ask a team admin to add it on the developer website.
diag.profileDevice.title: The provisioning profile does not include this device
diag.profileDevice.message: The current profile does not contain this device. With automatic signing, retry to regenerate it; with manual signing, add the device to the profile on the developer website and download it again.
diag.untrusted.title: The device does not trust this developer yet
diag.untrusted.message: The app is installed, but the first launch needs the developer to be trusted on the device: open Settings > General > VPN & Device Management, select the developer certificate and tap Trust, then retry.
diag.locked.title: The device is locked
diag.locked.message: Unlock the device and keep the screen on, then retry.
diag.busy.title: The device is being prepared for development
diag.busy.message: Xcode is preparing this device for development (for example copying symbols): {1}. Retry when it finishes; Xcode's Devices window shows the progress.
diag.destination.title: xcodebuild cannot find the device
diag.destination.message: The device may be locked, just disconnected, on an iOS version newer than this Xcode supports, or not yet prepared for development. Unlock it and retry; if it still fails, run on it from Xcode once.
diag.dbLocked.title: The build database is in use
diag.dbLocked.message: Xcode is building the same project (DerivedData is shared with Xcode). Retry after Xcode's build finishes, or stop the build in Xcode.
diag.spmResolve.title: Swift package resolution failed
diag.spmResolve.message: Usually the package repository (such as GitHub) is unreachable. Check the network or proxy and retry; you can also use File > Packages > Resolve Package Versions in Xcode.
diag.spmClone.title: Downloading Swift package {1} failed
diag.spmProduct.title: Missing Swift package product {1}
diag.platform.title: {1} platform is not installed
diag.platform.message: This Xcode is missing the iOS platform component. Download it here, or install it in Xcode > Settings > Components.
diag.podsSync.title: Pods are out of sync with Podfile.lock
diag.podVersions.title: CocoaPods cannot find compatible versions for {1}
diag.podVersions.message: The Podfile requirements conflict with Podfile.lock, or the local CocoaPods spec repo is outdated. Run pod repo update in Terminal and retry.
opt.showWarnings.info: By default only errors are shown and warnings are counted at the end of the build (Xcode’s Issue navigator lists them all). Turn on to print every warning while building.
build.warningsHidden: {0} compiler warnings not shown (turn on Show compiler warnings in the run configuration to see them)
